pr_body:
##### Summary
Fixes #6333 

The initial work was made on #6447, this PR is moving forward this work.

##### Component Name
proc.plugin
##### Test Plan

1 - Change your `netdata.conf` adding the following lines:

```
[plugin:proc:/proc/net/wireless]
        enable new interfaces detected at runtime = yes
        status for all interfaces = yes
        quality for all interfaces = yes
        discarded packets for all interfaces = yes
        missed for all interfaces = yes
```

2 - Compile this Branch on a computer with wireless.
3 - Start Netdata
4 - Set variable values to `no` inside your `netdata.conf` and check if the charts were disabled.

##### Additional Information
pr_comments: @thiagoftsm all metrics are absolute in the code, i suspect it is wrong (for example discarded packets, it is likely counter), we need to check it.

@thiagoftsm this info helps you to make charts titles better

- Status is the status reported by the modem.
- Link quality reports the quality of the modulation on the air (direct sequence spread spectrum).
- Level and Noise refer to the signal level and noise level.

I tried to find what is that status, but no luck.

It would be nice to have `filename to monitor` option for testing purposes. `mdstat` proc collector have it.

I am bringing the information  reported inside `man iwconfig`, I think they are clear enough to define our `title`.

> Why did you do that [`fb49748` (#10052)](https://github.com/netdata/netdata/pull/10052/commits/fb497488f93d19c0879435bc3998ff2553d65523)?

The original code never used that option, it looks like the developer had something in his mind, but he did not bring the feature. I also arrived in the conclusion that the code by default is adding and removing the interface when it is present or removed from the file, and I think this is the best monitoring we can do.

issue_context.title: wifi interface statistics (/proc/net/wireless )
issue_context.body:
##### Feature idea summary

`/proc/net/wireless` contains some useful info about wifi interfaces

```
[ilyam@ilyam-pc ~]$ cat /proc/net/wireless 
Inter-| sta-|   Quality        |   Discarded packets               | Missed | WE
 face | tus | link level noise |  nwid  crypt   frag  retry   misc | beacon | 22
wlp5s0: 0000   68.  -42.  -256        0      0      0      0   3851        0

```

related link: [link](https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/407775/how-is-proc-net-wireless-a-clone-of-proc-net-dev), [structiw__statistics](http://docs.ros.org/jade/api/heatmap/html/structiw__statistics.html)

##### Expected behavior

collect wifi statistics from `/proc/net/wireless`

 - `title`: The noise level indicates the amount of background noise in your environment. The closer the value to 0, the greater the noise level.
